# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Today's date]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination**
- **Member name:** Morgan Foster
- **Member ID:** W276906709
- **Reference number:** POC-EED29F7594-68772
- **Date of denial notice:** August 11, 2026
- **Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) that my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, requested on my behalf. The notice dated August 11, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records already in the file describe imaging findings at the most advanced grade used to measure arthritis.

## A note about the criteria quoted to me

I requested the clinical criteria used to decide my case. The policy identified is the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline named above. The specific criteria language I have been provided from that guideline addresses **shoulder** arthroplasty — for example:

> "shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:"

> "Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months' duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) *Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:"

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer: **no knee-specific criteria have been quoted to me**, so I cannot map my records line by line against the exact requirements that were applied to my request. I am not going to guess at policy language I have not seen. If Anthem relied on knee criteria within this guideline that I have not been shown, I ask that they be provided to me in writing so that I can respond to them directly.

What the language above does show is how the plan's own guideline treats Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 radiographs: within this guideline, grade 4 findings are written in as the exception that removes the need to satisfy the duration requirement. In the plan's own framework, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 is the point at which imaging is considered conclusive rather than borderline. The same guideline language also treats grade 4 as an exception to the conservative-management requirement:

> "Irregular joint surfaces Glenoid sclerosis Osteophyte changes Flattened glenoid Cystic changes in the humeral head Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes) Hemiarthroplasty Hemiarthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:"

## What my records show

The denial rests on imaging. Here is what the imaging in my file actually says, along with the rest of my record:

**Imaging (June 27, 2026 — MRI of the knee):** full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition; **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially**. Grade 4 is the highest grade on that scale. This is not an equivocal or early-arthritis finding.

**Duration of symptoms:** 14 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest.

**Conservative care already completed:**
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion — 16 weeks, February 25, 2026 through June 17, 2026, 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- Corticosteroid injection on March 26, 2026, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

**Functional impact:** I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times a night because of pain.

**Examination:** positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.

**Safety factors:** no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Taken together, the file documents advanced structural disease on imaging, symptoms lasting well over a year, a full and documented course of conservative treatment that did not work, and daily functional loss. I respectfully ask the reviewer to identify which specific imaging requirement was found unmet, because the imaging report in my file describes bone-on-bone apposition and the most severe radiographic grade available.

## What I am asking for

I ask Anthem to:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) requested by Dr. Lindqvist.
2. If the denial is maintained, provide me with the exact criteria from the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline that were applied to my knee arthroplasty request, and a written explanation of which specific imaging criterion my MRI of June 27, 2026 was found not to meet.
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery experience who has the complete record, including the MRI report and the physical therapy discharge note.

I understand this appeal must be received by **February 7, 2027**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also submit or follow up online at anthem.com or through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card.

Please contact me if any additional records would help. I am glad to have Dr. Lindqvist's office send anything further that is needed.

Thank you for your time and for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Foster**
Member ID: W276906709
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 11, 2026 (Reference POC-EED29F7594-68772)
- MRI report of the knee, June 27, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (February 25, 2026 – June 17, 2026, 24 visits)
- [Any additional records from Dr. Lindqvist's office]

Synovial fluid testing, such as leukocyte count and neutrophil percentage, aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures, leukocyte esterase, alpha defensin testing (Synovasure®), synovial fluid CRP, synovial fluid PCR for bacteria Intraoperative plan for histopathology and/or aerobic and anaerobic tissue cultures using implant sonication for cultures or PCR Contraindications All procedures listed in this guideline are contraindicated when ANY of the following conditions are present:
